messages:
Ingrid: Morning team, CI started failing across multiple repos ~07:00 UTC with 401s. Example runner log: `HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized\n\{\"error\":\"token_revoked\",\"message\":\"token was revoked\"\}`. We use a shared service account token stored in GH Secrets named REDWOOD_CI_TOKEN. Any idea what would revoke a token cluster-wide?

deploy-bot: :x: Job 9821 failed (integration) reason=401 token_revoked

Alex: thanks — can you paste the exact curl and the GH Actions step? Also was anything changed in token management/rotation in the last 48h?

Ingrid: curl we run from Actions:
```
curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_CI_TOKEN\" https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/health
```
GH action step:
```yaml
- name: smoke
  env:
    REDWOOD_CI_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.REDWOOD_CI_TOKEN }}
  run: |
    curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_CI_TOKEN\" https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/generate -d '{\"prompt\":\"ping\"}'
```

Maya (SRE): `token_revoked` usually means an admin action (revoke) or the service account was deactivated. I'll check audit logs. Priya, did infra run any mass-revoke or rotation window?

Priya (Infra): We did a rotation job last night aimed at stale personal tokens, but the rotation script selects tokens via a regex on creator metadata. It should have skipped tokens created by service accounts, but I see a pattern mismatch: bot user display names include the substring `-ci` and our script matched `-ci` as a candidate and revoked those tokens. Oops.

Alex: ok that explains the cause. Two immediate paths: 1) re-issue tokens and update GH Secrets, 2) for long-term, move org workflows to GitHub OIDC (no static tokens) or a short-lived token broker so we avoid static shared tokens.

Sam (DevEx): worth noting: for CI we recommend either
- federated credentials (GitHub OIDC) mapped to a Redwood service account, or
- per-repo service account tokens with least-privilege scopes and TTL 30d, rotated via an automation that updates secrets.
Switching to OIDC reduces blast radius of accidental revokes and removes secret handling.

Priya (Infra): pragmatic triage we did: recreated a bot service account `ci-bot-main`, minted a new token scoped only to `inference:generate` with TTL 7d and pushed it to the primary repo so the integration job can finish. We left the old tokens in revoked state.

Ingrid: created new secret REDWOOD_CI_TOKEN_V2 and pushed to 3 repos, smoke passes. But we have ~120 repos using the old secret. What's the plan to bulk update without adding risk?

Maya (SRE): two approaches:
- Write a small GH App that injects the new secret into repos where the app is installed (requires org-app permissions).
- Use a rotating proxy token endpoint (internal) that maps a single short-lived token to many consumers behind an allowlist. That reduces per-repo secrets but centralizes risk.

Alex: for short-term, do an incremental rollout: update top-traffic repos first, then the rest on a schedule. Priya, can infra run a `tokens:list` and `tokens:metadata` so we can audit which tokens got revoked and who owns them? Example admin API: 
```
# admin only
curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN\" https://admin.redwood-inference.internal/v1/service_accounts?filter=name:ci-bot
# tokens for an SA
curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN\" https://admin.redwood-inference.internal/v1/service_accounts/<SA_ID>/tokens
# token metadata
curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN\" https://admin.redwood-inference.internal/v1/tokens/<TOKEN_ID>/metadata
```

Priya (Infra): running those now. Audit shows ~130 tokens revoked by the rotation job between 2026-03-15T06:50 and 06:55 UTC. The job logfile shows it matched the regex `.*-ci.*` against creator_name; we'll patch it immediately to only match human-created tokens or specific personal namespaces.

SecurityBot: flagged the incident and raised a security ticket SEC-4761. Note: a shared long-lived CI token is a compliance concern. Recommend moving to per-repo tokens or OIDC.

Sam (DevEx): small checklist for remediation and hardening:
- Replace shared token with per-repo or OIDC-based auth (preferred).
- If static tokens remain, enforce least-privilege scopes (e.g., `inference:generate` only) and TTL <= 30d for non-federated tokens.
- Add an allowlist to rotation scripts and a dry-run mode (do not revoke automatically unless confirmed).
- Add console warning when creating long-lived non-human tokens.
- Add alerting for spikes in `token_revoked` errors across customers.

Alex: can we add an internal KB entry with migration steps from static token -> GitHub OIDC? Also add a tiny rotation helper script that: create->verify->update-secret->revoke old.

Ingrid: I'll coordinate repo updates and will open a PR for the rotation helper. Priya, please post the patched rotation job and the debug log so we can audit.

Priya (Infra): patched rotation job (now matches only `created_by_type:personal`) and posted log to the infra ticket. Also we added a safeguard: rotation will now run in `--dry-run` by default for 24h after changes.

Maya (SRE): follow-ups:
- SRE: add an alert rule for >5% 401s with `token_revoked` across orgs.
- DevEx: publish OIDC migration KB and an example IAM mapping.
- Infra: roll out patched rotation and run audit job to recreate revoked service-account tokens where needed.

Ingrid: all good — thanks. New token rollout reduced failures to 0. I'm updating on-call docs to prefer OIDC and to include the create->verify->rotate sequence.

Alex: closing for now. If anyone sees other unexpected 401s, ping @sre-oncall and re-open. :thumbsup:

Attachments:
- rotation job log: https://logs.internal/rotation/2026-03-15
- admin token docs: https://internal.redwood/docs/admin/tokens
- KB draft: https://docs.redwood-internal/support/ci-token-migration
